questions.question: A man invested ₹4,500 at 5% per annum and ₹5,500 at 8% per annum simple interest. Both investments were for 4 years each. The amount received from the lower rate of interest is what per cent (rounded off to the nearest integer) of the amount received from the higher rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Given:

**Case 1:**

P = 4,500, R = 5%, t= 4 yr

**Case 2:**

P = 5,500, R = 8%, t = 4 yr

Formula used:

Simple interest = P × R × T / 100 [ P = principal, R = rate of interest, T = time]

Amount = Principal + SI

Calculation:

**Case 1: **

⇒ SI = (4500 × 5 × 4) / 100 = 900

⇒ Amount = 4500 + 900 = 5400

Case 2: 

⇒ SI = (5500 × 8 × 4) / 100 = 1760

⇒ Amount = 5500 + 1760 = 7260

The required percentage will be (5400/7260) × 100

⇒ 74% (approx.)

questions.question: A man invested a total of Rs.12,050 in two parts, one at 10% p.a. simple interest for 2 years and the other at the same rate at compound interest, interest being compounded annually, for the same time. The amounts he received from both the parts are equal. The sum (in Rs.) invested at the compound interest is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total investment = Rs.12050

Rate of interest = 10% 

Time = 2 years 

**Formulas used:**

Simple Interest = Principal × Time × Rate/100 

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest 

In Compound Interest; Amount = Principal × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculation:**

Let the sum invested at compound interest be = y 

⇒ Sum invested at simple interest = 12050 - y 

As per the question;

(12050 - y) + (12050 - y) × 10/100 × 2 = y × (1 + 10/100)²

⇒ (12050 - y) [1 + 1/5] = y × 11/10 × 11/10 

⇒ (12050 - y) × 6/5 = y × 121/100 

⇒ 12050 × 6/5 - y × 6/5 = y × 121/100 

⇒14460 = 121y/100 + 6y/5

⇒ 14460 = (121y + 120y)/100 

⇒ 14460 = 241y/100 

⇒y = (14460 × 100)/241 

⇒ y = 6000 

**∴ The sum invested on compound interest is Rs.6000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Equivalent rate of interest in the case of CI 

⇒ 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%

Let a and b be the sum invested on SI and CI.

a + (a × 2 × 10)/100 = b + (b × 21)/100

⇒ a/b = 121/120

(121 + 120) units = 12050

⇒ 241 units = 12050

⇒ 1 unit = 12050/241 = 50

The sum invested on CI = 120 units = 50 × 120

⇒ Rs. 6000

 The sum invested on compound interest is Rs.6000.

questions.question: A certain sum becomes Rs. 13650 at 15% p.a. simple interest after 2 years. What will be the amount (in Rs.) of the same sum after 1 year at the same rate of interest, if the interest is compounded half yearly? (nearest to a Rs.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amount = Rs. 13650

Rate of Interest = 15%

Time = 2 Years

**Formula used:**

S.I = PRT/100

Amount = Principal + S.I

**Calculation:**

Let the Principal be Rs. x

S.I = Rs. (13650 – x)

According to the question,

⇒ (x × 15 × 2)/100 = 13650 – x

⇒ 3x/10 = 13650 – x

⇒ 3x = 136500 – 10x

⇒ 13x = 136500

⇒ x = 10500

Now, if rate of interest is compounded half yearly, the interest becomes half and Time becomes twice

So, Rate of interest = 15% ÷ 2 = 7.5%

Time period = 1 × 2 = 2 years

Now, amount after 1 year = Rs. 10500 × (107.5/100)²

⇒ Rs. 12134.0625 ≈ Rs. 12134

**∴ Amount becomes Rs. 12134 after 1 year if compounded half yearly**

questions.question: Peter invested a certain sum of money in a scheme paying 10% simple interest per annum, while Rachel invested half of the sum that Peter invested in a scheme paying 10% interest per annum compounded annually. Also, while Peter invested for 2 years, Rachel invested for 3 years. If the difference in the interest earned by Peter and Rachel was Rs. 897, what was the sum that Rachel had invested?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Peter's Rate of Simple Interest (SI) = 10% per annum

Rachel's Rate of Compound Interest (CI) = 10% per annum, compounded annually

Peter's investment duration = 2 years

Rachel's investment duration = 3 years

Difference in interest earned by Peter and Rachel = Rs. 897

Rachel's principal = 1/2 of Peter's principal

**Formulas:**

Simple Interest (SI) = PRT/100

Compound Interest (CI) = P[(1 + (r)/(100))^t - 1]

**Calculation:**

Let's denote Peter's principal (the sum he invested) as (P).

SI = (Ptimes 2×10)/(100) = (P)/(5)

Rachel's principal = (P/2)

CI = (P)/(2)[(1 + (10)/(100))³ - 1]

CI = (P)/(2)[((11)/(10))³ - 1] = (P)/(2)[0.331]

Interest Difference = 897

⇒ (P)/(5) - (P)/(2)[0.331] = 897

⇒ (2P-1.655P)/(10) = 897

⇒ (0.345P)/(10) = 897 

⇒ P = Rs. 26000

The sum that Rachel had invested =P/2 = 26000/2 = Rs. 13,000.

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 12,000 is invested for 15 months at 10% per annum compounded half yearly. What is the percentage gain, at the end of 15 months, correct to one decimal place?
questions.solution:
Suppose P = Principal, R = rate of interest and N = time

Compound interest calculated half yearly = P(1 + (R/2)/100)²ⁿ – 1

Given,

Time = 1 year and 3 months

Amount = 12000(1 + 5/100)² = 13230

Simple Interest = (13230 × 3/12 × 10)/100 = 330.75

Amount after 15 months = 13230 + 330.75 = Rs.13560.75

Percentage increase = (13560.75 – 12000) / (12000) × 100 = 13.0%

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum of Rs. 8,000 at a certain rate per cent per annum for 3 years is Rs. 3,600. What will be the amount (in Rs.) of the same sum after 2 years at the same rate, if the interest is compounded 8-monthly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T) = (3600 × 100) ÷ (8000 × 3) = 15% p.a.

For 8-monthly compounding, cycle rate = 15% × (8 ÷ 12) = 10% per 8 months.

Total time of 2 years = 24 months, which gives 24 ÷ 8 = 3 compounding cycles.

Amount after 3 cycles at 10% growth = 8000 × (11/10)³

Amount = 8000 × 1.331 = 10648.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,648.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹8000

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹3600

Time for SI (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Compound Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fcc831dde7e4c41909fdfb4dcf624e5fe21d461c00ed095de0a5fea2029a80db.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 3600 = (8000 × R × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 3600 = 240 × R

⇒ R = 15% per annum

⇒ The rate for an 8-monthly period = 15% × (8 ÷ 12) = 10%

⇒ Time duration = 2 years = 24 months

⇒ Number of 8-monthly cycles (n) = 24 ÷ 8 = 3

⇒ Total Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

⇒ Total Amount = 8000 × (1 + 10/100)³

⇒ Total Amount = 8000 × (11/10) × (11/10) × (11/10)

⇒ Total Amount = 8000 × (1331 ÷ 1000)

⇒ Total Amount = 8 × 1331 = 10648

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,648.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Compounding Rate

When interest is compounded k-monthly, the applicable rate per cycle becomes R% × (k ÷ 12) and total cycles become Total Months ÷ k.

Compound vs Simple Interest Difference

For 2 years, CI − SI = P(R/100)². For 3 years, CI − SI = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Compounding Frequencies

If compounded Half-yearly: Rate is halved, time cycles are doubled. If Quarterly: Rate becomes one-fourth, time cycles become four times.

questions.question: A borrowed a sum of Rs. 160000 from B at 10% per annum simple interest. At the same time he lent the same sum to C at the same rate on compound interest, compounded semi-annually for 2 years, Find the amount (in Rs.) earned by A in the whole transaction.
questions.solution:
** Given:**

Principal = Rs. 160000

Rate = 10%

Time = 2 years

**Formula used:**

SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P × (1 + r/100)t

CI = Amount – Principal

When compound semi-annually, r' = r/2 and t' = 2 × t

**Calculation:**

According to the question

SI = (160000 × 10 × 2)/100

⇒ Rs. 32000

Now,

Compounded amount when compounded semi annually = P(1 + r/200)² × t

Compounded amount = 160000[1 + 10/200)² × ²

⇒ 160000(21/20)⁴

⇒ Rs. (160000 × 21/20 × 21/20 × 21/20 × 21/20)

⇒ Rs. 194481

CI = Amount – Principal = (194481 – 160000)

⇒ Rs. 34481

Now, the amount earned by A in the whole transaction = CI – SI

⇒ (34481 – 32000)

⇒ Rs. 2481

**∴ Required amount earned by A in the whole transaction is 2481**

questions.question: A sum amounts to Rs. 6580 in 2 years and amounts to Rs. 7896 in 3 years on compound interest (compounding annually) at the same rate of interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

If the sum amounts to Rs. 6580 in 2 years and Rs. 7896 in 3 years, the difference (Rs. 7896 - Rs. 6580 = Rs. 1316) would be the interest earned in the third year.

So, the interest for the third year, Rs. 1316, was obtained from the amount that was there at the end of two years, which is Rs. 6580.

Interest for third year = Sum after 2 years × annual interest rate

1316 = 6580 × r

Solving this equation for r gives us:

r = 1316/6580 × 100 = 20%

**So, the annual rate of interest is 20%.**
